free_tier.stated: Send Large Files - Free File Sharing and Transfer up to 10 GB. No Email Required.

retention.stated: unverified: expiry is an option ('optionally with a password or an expiry date'), no default period is published

egress.terms: No byte allowance stated. The page offers a download limit and revocation per transfer, so traffic out is controlled by the sender rather than metered by the vendor.

interface_detail: Browser drop zone. /api/upload returns 404, /api/files returns 400, so a JSON API exists (the 400 is a validation answer) but its contract is not published.
tooling: Browser only as observed. The 400 from /api/files is the one opening: it means a JSON endpoint answers, and a wrapper could probe it.
chaining: A per-transfer download limit and revocation make it a controlled hand-off, which is the opposite of a mirror; it does not chain into an archive.

limits.value: sender can set a download limit per transfer

limits_note: Revocation and per-download visibility are the differentiators the page sells; neither was exercised.
binding_note: The publishable download limit is the first constraint a re-fetch meets: a link with a limit of one is spent by the first reader, and at 1 TiB a month that means a new transfer per read.

identity_cost.detail: 'No accounts, no ads: Nobody needs to sign up, neither you nor your recipients'

reliability_note: No published operator, no API documentation, and an edge that answers unknown POSTs with 404.
confidence_note: The 10 GB offer and the no-account sentence are quoted from the vendor page; nothing was uploaded, so the cap is the page's word.

evidence.proved: 'Free File Sharing and Transfer up to 10 GB', 'No accounts, no ads: Nobody needs to sign up, neither you nor your recipients', and the password / download-limit / revocation options
HTTP 400 from a JSON endpoint at /api/files, so an API exists but publishes no contract

notes: The controlled-hand-off feature set is real but unmeasured; the record exists so the next session does not re-discover the name.
